questions.questionText: How does a single artificial neuron relate to something from the Classical ML course?
options: It's unrelated to anything covered previously
A single neuron (weighted sum + sigmoid) is mathematically the same computation as logistic regression
It's the same as a decision tree split
It's equivalent to a full random forest
questions.correctAnswer: A single neuron (weighted sum + sigmoid) is mathematically the same computation as logistic regression
questions.explanation: A neuron computes a weighted sum plus bias, then squashes it with an activation function — exactly logistic regression's z = w*x + b followed by sigmoid.

questions.questionText: Why is a nonlinear activation function between layers essential, rather than optional?
options: It's purely cosmetic and doesn't affect what the network can learn
Without nonlinearity, stacking many linear layers mathematically collapses to a single linear layer, so depth alone buys no extra representational power
It only matters for the output layer, not hidden layers
It's needed only to speed up training, not to change what's learnable
questions.correctAnswer: Without nonlinearity, stacking many linear layers mathematically collapses to a single linear layer, so depth alone buys no extra representational power
questions.explanation: A composition of purely linear transformations is still just a linear transformation — nonlinear activations are what let depth actually add representational capacity.

questions.questionText: What computation does a "forward pass" refer to?
options: Updating the network's weights based on an error signal
Propagating an input through the network, layer by layer, to produce an output prediction
Splitting the dataset into train and test sets
Selecting which activation function to use
questions.correctAnswer: Propagating an input through the network, layer by layer, to produce an output prediction
questions.explanation: The forward pass is purely computing the output from a given input using the network's current weights — no learning happens during it, that's the subject of the backpropagation lesson.
